module_title: Union Executive - Powers, Duties, and Election Nuances
introduction: At this level, we explore the specific constitutional powers of the President (Legislative, Executive, Judicial), the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers, and the specific methods of election and removal for the top offices.

core_concepts.title: Presidential Powers
core_concepts.description: 1. Executive: Appoints PM, Ministers, CAG, Governors, etc. 2. Legislative: Summons/Prorogues Parliament, addresses first session, issues Ordinances (Art 123). 3. Judicial: Appoints SC/HC judges, Pardoning power (Art 72).

core_concepts.title: Impeachment of the President (Article 61)
core_concepts.description: The President can be removed only for 'Violation of the Constitution'. The process can start in either House. It requires a 14-day notice and a resolution passed by a 2/3rd majority of the TOTAL membership of both Houses.

core_concepts.title: Collective Responsibility (Article 75)
core_concepts.description: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means the ministry stays in power as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

core_concepts.title: Ordinance Making Power (Article 123)
core_concepts.description: The President can promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. It has the same force as an Act but must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembly.

important_entities.name: Pardoning Power (Article 72)
important_entities.significance: Includes Pardon, Commutation, Remission, Respite, and Reprieve. Unlike Governors, the President can pardon a death sentence.

important_entities.name: Attorney General (Article 76)
important_entities.significance: The highest law officer in the country, appointed by the President. He has the right to speak in both Houses but no right to vote.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: When the VP acts as President, he ceases to perform the duties of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha. His duties there are performed by the Deputy Chairman.
Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) vote in the President's election but have NO role in his impeachment or in the VP's election.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Pardon, Commutation, Remission, Respite, Reprieve. (Pardon is total freedom; Commutation is changing the nature of punishment).

exam_strategy_tips: Note that 'Violation of the Constitution' is not defined in the Constitution.
The President can only issue an ordinance on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
